title: NY State Senate · District 59
area: Parts of western Queens (including Long Island City and Astoria), northern Brooklyn, and the east side of Manhattan.

context.text: Incumbent Kristen Gonzalez is unopposed on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot; the Republican primary for this seat was canceled with no candidate advancing, and Gonzalez advanced on both the Democratic and Working Families lines without appearing on a primary ballot.

candidates.name: Kristen Gonzalez
candidates.currentRole: New York State Senator, District 59 (since January 2023)

summary.text: Kristen Gonzalez is the Democratic and Working Families Party candidate for re-election to New York State Senate District 59, running unopposed. She has represented the district since January 2023 and chairs the Senate Elections Committee and the Senate Internet and Technology Committee.

background.text: Born and raised in Queens, New York, in a working-class family; lives in Long Island City.
Worked as a legislative staffer for the New York City Council, the Obama White House, and Senator Chuck Schumer's office before running for office.
Organized with the Western Queens Community Land Trust and served on her local community board.
The youngest woman ever elected to the New York State Senate.
Chairs the Senate Elections Committee and the Senate Internet and Technology Committee in the 2025–2026 session.

priorities.text: Her legislative focus includes protecting abortion rights through health-data privacy safeguards.
Her legislative focus includes regulating government use of artificial intelligence and securing elections against deceptive media.
She describes herself as championing workers' rights, affordable housing, tenant protections, and a "Green New York."

positions.summary: Sponsored the Responsible Data Center Development Act (S10642), which sets a 90%-by-2040 renewable-energy target tied to data-center electricity use and passed the Senate 43–17 on June 4, 2026.
Voted yes on S8455-B, which passed the Senate 56–4 and creates new criminal offenses restricting the sale of flare guns.

Sponsored the Youth Employment Empowerment Act (S10485), a pilot rental-assistance program for public-housing families who risk losing housing subsidies because a household member under 21 earns income.
Her official priorities include protecting abortion rights through health-data privacy protections.

record.text: Sponsored the Responsible Data Center Development Act (S10642), setting renewable-energy targets and utility rate classifications for large data centers; passed the Senate 43–17 on June 4, 2026 and was substituted by an Assembly version that passed the same day. Not yet signed as of September 2026.

Sponsored the Homegrown Energy Act (S10546), which would require hyperscale data centers to fund household electrification in their host communities; remained in the Senate Energy and Telecommunications Committee as of May 20, 2026.
Sponsored S10675, imposing liability on chatbot operators that let their systems impersonate licensed professionals; remained in the Senate Rules Committee as of August 5, 2026.

Sponsored S10599, requiring officials served with subpoenas or warrants for election materials to notify the Attorney General and State Board of Elections within 36 hours; remained in the Senate Elections Committee as of May 29, 2026.

Sponsored the Youth Employment Empowerment Act (S10485), a four-year pilot rental-subsidy program for public-housing families; introduced May 15, 2026 and remained in the Senate Housing, Construction and Community Development Committee.
Chairs the Senate Elections Committee and the Senate Internet and Technology Committee for the 2025–2026 legislative session.
Voted yes on S8455-B, restricting the sale of flare guns, which passed the Senate 56–4 on June 1, 2026.
